sources.entry: Thread management - Sets the physical-core default, the affinity it implies and the spin-wait controls that trade idle CPU for latency.

summary.title: Thread management
summary.one_liner: Learn how to tune ONNX Runtime CPU threading: intra-op and inter-op thread counts, thread affinity, spin-wait controls, NUMA placement, and custom thread callbacks.
keywords: how many threads for onnx inference
reduce cpu usage of idle threads
takeaways: By default intra_op_num_threads is 0, which sets the intra-op thread count to the number of physical cores and enables some affinitization.
Setting intra_op_num_threads explicitly disables affinity for the created threads; affinities can be set with session.intra_op_thread_affinities.
Spinning (allow_spinning) gives faster inference at the cost of CPU cycles and power; spin_duration_us and spin_backoff_max bound and reduce that cost.
ORT_PARALLEL execution mode with inter_op_num_threads helps models with many branches but may hurt models without them.
On NUMA systems, test several thread settings; the page reports nearly 20% improvement when affinities are limited to one NUMA node in its test.
summary.summary: This ONNX Runtime docs page explains the CPU execution provider's threading knobs, starting with defaults in Python (intra_op_num_threads=0, ORT_SEQUENTIAL, ORT_ENABLE_ALL). It covers intra-op threads (parallelism within an operator), inter-op threads (parallelism across operators, used only in parallel mode), and how thread affinity is set by default and by session config keys. It then describes spin-wait controls (allow_spinning, spin_duration_us, spin_backoff_max), NUMA considerations, C++ custom thread creation and join callbacks for session and global pools, and use of the intra-op pool from custom ops. Code examples are given in Python and C++.
